subject: Environment proofing & account setup — Preflight checklist and deliverables
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@acmehealth.com>, ops+onboard@acmehealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Environment proofing & account setup — Preflight checklist and deliverables

Hi Jordan / Acme onboarding team,

Great to kick off the private deployment intake. Attached is a short preflight worksheet (redwood-private-preflight.xlsx) that helps us validate account-level prerequisites and environment readiness before we schedule Day 0. Can you confirm the items below by end of week?

Summary asks (short):
- Provide public egress IP(s) or CIDR blocks we'll see traffic from (for allowlist).
- Confirm KMS provider and key rotation/rotation windows (if using customer KMS).
- Share the environment inventory PDF (OS versions, hypervisor, VLAN mapping).
- Designate a primary SRE contact and a network person for test window.
- Expected steady-state QPS and any large-burst traffic patterns.

Attachments: redwood-private-preflight.xlsx (worksheet), onboarding-playbook-v1.pdf (link in Drive).

If anything looks unclear I can hop on a 30m call with your SRE and network folks tomorrow afternoon — otherwise please fill the sheet and return. Once we have those, Ben and Karthik will propose a Day 0 date and a short smoke-test plan.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-private-preflight.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Oct 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Environment proofing & account setup — Preflight checklist and deliverables

Marissa — thanks, received. We're glad to get this moving.

Quick answers:
- Egress CIDR: 34.85.120.0/24 (primary), we may add another /24 for burst windows.
- KMS: We use AWS KMS (key alias arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:alias/acme-key), rotation monthly.
- Inventory: attached acme-environment-inventory.pdf (includes hostnames, VLAN tags, hypervisor versions).
- Primary SRE: Jordan Lee (me); Network owner: Priyanka Singh (priya.singh@acmehealth.com).
- Traffic: baseline 350 QPS, expected spike to 1.2k QPS during batch jobs (approx 2x short bursts).

We have a compliance question: does Redwood require SOC2 evidence for the private control plane, or is our MSA and the shared evidence portal sufficient? Attaching the inventory now.

Jordan
Jordan Lee, Senior SRE — Acme Health
jordan@acmehealth.com

Attachment: acme-environment-inventory.pdf (PDF, 128KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@acmehealth.com>, ops+onboard@acmehealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Oct 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Environment proofing & account setup — Preflight checklist and deliverables

Thanks Jordan — that inventory is perfect. Short answers on compliance: for Private (VPC) deployments we typically need either (A) customer acceptance of the MSA + shared evidence package (portal link), or (B) a SOC 2 report if the customer has an internal policy requiring that. For Acme Health I think the MSA + portal will suffice; I'll loop in our security reviewer if you require a signed attestation.

Next technical preflight items (from the worksheet, for clarity):
- BGP/Peering: confirm ASN and whether you prefer static peering vs. BGP (we support both; BGP preferred for failover).
- MTU and jumbo frames: will you require >1500? If so, list target MTU and affected VLANs.
- NAT & egress: confirm whether you will SNAT at your edge or expect us to provide NAT.
- Service account and IAM: create redwood-onboard@acmehealth.com (AWS) with limited role for onboarding (we only need List/Describe for initial checks).

Proposed Day 0: Nov 7, 2028 — Ben and Karthik will lead the wire-up and a 2-hour smoke test (routing, egress, KMS connectivity). Can you confirm availability for Nov 7–9 window?

Link: Private deployment onboarding playbook (internal) — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d

Marissa

---
Attachment: onboarding-playbook-v1.pdf (link; 2MB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Oct 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Environment proofing & account setup — Preflight checklist and deliverables

Jordan — noted on CIDR and KMS. A couple of technical clarifications before Day 0:

- Peering: preference is to do BGP with ASNs exchanged. Please share your ASN and keep BGP timers at default for now; we'll tune if we see flaps.
- MTU: If you are using jumbo frames for storage networks, restrict jumbo to storage VLANs; control plane interfaces should remain 1500 to avoid fragmentation with our managed NAT path.
- TCP keepalive: for long streaming sessions (LLM inference) we recommend 60s keepalive and idle timeouts >5m in your edge ALB/firewall.
- Health checks: provide a small test token so we can run a token-level smoke that validates KMS wrap/unwrap and token acceptance.

I'll schedule a 45m tech sync with Karthik and your network lead — proposing Oct 30 10:00 PDT.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Environment proofing & account setup — Preflight checklist and deliverables

Looping in schedule and the technical checklist I'll run on Day 0. Jordan / Priyanka — can you confirm the following by COB Monday?

Day 0 checklist (technical):
- ASN: please confirm (required for BGP).
- BFD: optional; if enabled, we'll test with conservative timers.
- MTU: confirm per-VLAN expectations (we'll mark control plane 1500).
- KMS endpoint: provide endpoint and test credentials (short-lived) for wrap/unwrap.
- DNS: add ad-hoc A records for the smoke endpoints (we'll provide names).
- Baseline QPS: confirm (you noted 350 steady, 1.2k spikes) — we'll size initial batch/concurrency accordingly.

Config recommendation (short):
- initial_batch_size: 8
- max_concurrency_per_gpu: 6
- fallback_model_variant: quantized-8bit (for burst fallback)

We can run a canary with 15 minutes of synthetic traffic before full smoke. If Nov 7 still works for the team, we'll treat Nov 7 as target Day 0 and Nov 8 as backup.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
